subject.title: fix(sms): ack rate-limited Twilio callbacks instead of dropping them [AI]

question: Should an authenticated SMS callback above the dispatch quota remain an explicit HTTP 429 rejection, or should OpenClaw add durable deferred acceptance before returning HTTP 200?
rationale: This determines whether OpenClaw promises message acceptance under overload; changing that contract cannot be resolved by tests or a mechanical patch alone.

options.title: Keep explicit rejection
options.body: Retain HTTP 429 for callbacks OpenClaw cannot accept and rely on documented retry or fallback configuration.

options.title: Add durable deferred delivery
options.body: Persist validated callbacks in a bounded durable queue and return HTTP 200 only after the write commits.

options.title: Accept intentional loss
options.body: Approve HTTP 200 ack-and-drop as product policy with explicit loss metrics, operator documentation, and exact live proof.

recommendation.title: Keep explicit rejection
recommendation.body: Retain HTTP 429 for callbacks OpenClaw cannot accept and rely on documented retry or fallback configuration.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work established the current callback quota and rejection behavior, making them the strongest available history-based routing candidate.
